newsitem.title: FRANCE: YACHTING-FIRST SATELLITE PHOTOS TAKEN FOR MISSING CANADIAN.
newsitem.headline: YACHTING-FIRST SATELLITE PHOTOS TAKEN FOR MISSING CANADIAN.

text.p: The first radar satellite photos were taken on Sunday of a vast area of icy Antarctic seas where Canadian yachtsman Gerry Roufs has been missing since Tuesday in the dramatic Vendee Globe sailing challenge, organisers said.
"The first pictures were taken around 1200 GMT and beamed to Canada where they will be interpreted. We should get the results tomorrow," a spokeswoman said.

The search for Roufs was temporarily suspended earlier in the day because a cargo vessel scouring the area was running out of fuel but another vessel may be asked to enter the area in the next few hours, the spokeswoman said.

The area over which the satellite took its pictures was in one of the world's most isolated maritime zones with closest land -- French Polynesia, Chile and New Zealand -- all more than 2,500 nautical miles away.
The area is too far from land for the Australian air force, which dramatically rescued two other competitors in the race, to intervene.
The Australian naval vessel HMAS Adelaide was meanwhile heading home with two yachtsmen its helicopter plucked from the sea after they were spotted by Australian planes after several days at sea.
Briton Tony Bullimore, 56, was rescued on Thursday after surviving for four days in an air pocket in his upturned yacht, battered by high seas 2,600 km (1,600 miles) from Australia.
The Adelaide also rescued French yachtsman Thierry Dubois, a competitor in the same race.
The yachts of both Dubois and Bullimore capsized in heavy seas.
